themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

hero.oneLiner: The deck positions The Hi-Tech Gears Ltd. as a 39-year-old, dual-shore auto component maker of high-precision gears, shafts and transmission/engine components, supplying marquee global OEMs from 5 plants (3 in India, 1 each in Canada and USA) while its India business runs a consolidation-and-efficiency transformation.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Incorporated in 1986, THGL describes itself as an auto component manufacturer of high repute supplying engine and transmission components to marquee customers globally, and a key strategic supplier to various automotive OEMs.
- Deck claims it is 'one of the very few component manufacturers catering to diverse segments of automobiles and engines' — Two-Wheeler, Passenger Vehicles, Commercial Vehicles On-Highway, and Agri/Off-Highway.
- Named customers include Hero MotoCorp, Daimler, Cummins, Robert Bosch, JCB, New Holland, M&M, Honda Car, Magna Powertrain, American Axle, GKN, BorgWarner, Dana, Navistar and Stackpole across India, USA, Brazil and other geographies; exports to 10+ countries.
- FY26 consolidated revenue contribution by segment: Passenger Vehicles 40%, Two Wheelers 31%, Commercial Vehicles and Off-Highway 29%. FY26 revenue contribution by geography: India 54%, International 46% (deck footnotes International as 'Exports + North America Sub').
- 'Dual shore presence' — India plants at Bhiwadi (Est. 1986), Manesar (Est. 2005) and Bhiwadi Plant-III (Est. 2011); overseas plants at Guelph, Canada and Emporium, USA, both acquired in 2017.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Net Debt to Equity has been reduced over three years: 0.30x (FY24), 0.09x (FY25), 0.05x (FY26); the snapshot slide headlines 0.05x Net Debt/Equity.
- Consolidated non-current borrowings fell from INR 530 Mn (FY24) to INR 217 Mn (FY25) to INR 74 Mn (FY26), and current borrowings from INR 1,416 Mn to INR 594 Mn to INR 534 Mn; standalone non-current borrowings are 0 in FY26.
- Snapshot slide headlines ROCE of 7.41%; the historical chart shows ROCE of 28.58% (FY24), 13.59% (FY25), 7.41% (FY26) with the deck noting FY24 was flattered by a one-time income of INR 772 Mn in the overseas subsidiary in Q2 FY24.
- Cash Conversion Cycle (Days) is charted as 70 (FY24), 90 (FY25), 98 (FY26) — i.e. lengthening working capital.
- Consolidated equity grew INR 4,662 Mn (FY24) to INR 4,836 Mn (FY25) to INR 5,226 Mn (FY26); the deck discloses no dividend or buyback policy.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Impairment] Other Comprehensive Income in FY25 includes a loss of Rs 116.20 million on account of impairment in fair valuation of the investment in equity shares of Altigreen Propulsion Labs Private Limited, based on a registered valuer's share valuation report.
- [One-off] The deck notes higher Net Profit, ROCE and ROE in FY24 were due to a one-time income of INR 772 Mn in the overseas subsidiary in Q2 FY24 (shown as Exceptional Items of INR 770 Mn in FY24).
- [Order pipeline] A new business LOI was received from a new customer described as a market leader in the premium motorcycle segment in India; the RFQ pipeline includes active RFQs in two-wheeler and passenger car segments from both new and existing customers.
- [North America] North American business revenues increased both sequentially and year-on-year, with market demand stabilizing as geo-political uncertainty is factored in; new business was won in Q2 FY26 with two existing customers and samples are being made for PPAP approval.
- [Governance/Shareholding] Board includes seven independent directors; shareholding as on 30th June 2026 is Promoters 56.12% and Public 43.88%, with 18.79 Mn shares outstanding.
